title: Clean replay of the historical Cicada 3301 OpenPGP artifact verification
claim: On the declared Windows environment, the public verifier reproduced the recorded SHA-256 identity and both recorded OpenPGP fingerprints for the bundled historical key artifact.
why_it_matters: It supplies a complete public run behind OBS-0001 and demonstrates the difference between verifying artifact identity and claiming present-day authority.
scope: The bytes in keys/cicada-3301-2012.asc and fingerprint fields in keys/manifest.json only; no message signature, account, or HMS affiliation is authenticated.
method: Execute the public verifier under ENV-0002. It calculates the artifact SHA-256, asks GnuPG to parse primary and subkey fingerprints, and compares both results with the public manifest.
controls: The verifier rejects a file-hash mismatch before fingerprint comparison and compares the ordered parsed fingerprint list with the declared manifest values.
reproduction: From the repository root, run `python scripts/verify_cicada_key.py`. Expected output: `PASS — SHA-256 and 2 OpenPGP fingerprint(s) match the manifest.`
limitations: This is an artifact-identity reproduction, not a Liber Primus plaintext result.
A public-key fingerprint does not prove possession of the private key or present-day authority.
The intake history before the bundled bytes remains bounded by the limitations in OBS-0001.
